## Painted Porch Strategies (PPS): operating context

This project is the Painted Porch Strategies website. It is Painted Porch Strategies' own space, with its own website, code, database and client
delivery. Other businesses in the portfolio have their own projects: never bring their branding,
voice or data in here.

### Client records

Every business in the portfolio is moving off GoHighLevel (GHL), the CRM in use today, to
self-managed CRM and marketing. Don't build anything new on GHL: no new pipeline, nurture,
lead-generation, or client or resource delivery features. Existing GHL writes keep running until
they are migrated. Change them only to keep them working.

New intake and lead capture from this site goes to the PPS Ops Hub, Painted Porch Strategies' own operations platform, not to GHL.

Whatever system holds client records:

- One person, one record: match on email so you never create a duplicate. An email typed into a form doesn't prove who sent it, so an unverified submission may add to an existing record but never overwrite or remove what is there.
- On every contact, keep the email, the brand ("Painted Porch Strategies"), the source (which page or form), the date, and any consent exactly as the person gave it. Brand and source are fields, never tags. A deal belongs to one brand ("Painted Porch Strategies").
- Choose pipelines and stages by ID, never by name.
- Keep CRM and API keys server-side (edge or server functions only), never in browser code.
- Never copy another business's client records into this project.

### Business decisions

A decision that concerns only Painted Porch Strategies, such as its own offers, pricing, or a tool
only PPS uses, is recorded in the PPS Ops Hub's decision register. A decision that affects another
business or the whole portfolio, such as shared tools, roles or accounts, is made in the portfolio's
internal operations hub. If a request would change one of these, flag it instead of deciding it in
code.

### Knowledge-base publication

Every Google Doc used as an Ops Hub knowledge-base view must have a substantive, committed repository source. The repository is authoritative; the Doc is a supporting visual view. Use native Google Docs, not uploaded Word or Markdown files. Keep source path, full commit, version/status and source/view links aligned. Project snapshots are dated references: check current repository main and the linked Doc before relying on a current decision. Deliver repository and native-Doc links by default, not ZIP or Word exports.

# Project rules
- Website imagery follows PPS-DEC-0023 in the PPS Ops Hub (`docs/decisions/PPS-DEC-0023-website-imagery-rules.md`): never an AI-generated face; hands or other parts of a figure with no face showing are allowed; otherwise use abstract imagery, objects and scenes; no cartoon-style images; each image on one page only. Real photos of the real team are allowed. The speaking hero, four workshop thumbnails and talk covers are existing exceptions listed in the record; don't add to them. Why: PPS Admin set these rules on 2026-11-05, restated them on 2026-11-07, and the same day narrowed the people rule to faces ("passenger to pilot only has hands, that's ok and allowed. It's just not faces"). Check every candidate image before proposing it, unused files included. Unused files showing AI-generated faces, among them portraits named after Amy, Rob and Sierra that were not them, were deleted on 2026-11-07 at PPS Admin's request.

- Buttons and form fields have 4px corners: plain `rounded` on every link or button drawn as a button (solid fill or outline) and on every text field, text area, select and date picker. The shared `Button`, `Input`, `Textarea` and `SelectTrigger` carry it. Use `rounded`, not `rounded-md` or `rounded-lg`: those follow the theme's `--radius`, which differs inside and outside the new design. One exception: the header's Find Your Next ShIFt stays a pill, matching the pill-shaped header bar it sits in. Cards and callout boxes stay square; topic tags and filter chips stay pills; the guide's answer cards and the Results & Impact logo cards are cards, not buttons. Archived and unused pages are left as they are. Why: PPS-DEC-0028; PPS Admin, 2026-11-07, first "all cta buttons ... straight with no rounded corners", then choosing a compromise between square and pill: "4px on all buttons and form fields, with the header button staying a pill? yes", and of cards and callout boxes, "Id like to keep them square for now". Tests in `src/components/v3/__tests__/SiteChrome.test.tsx`.

- Button text on the public site is set in spaced capitals with the `cta-label` class (`src/styles/v3.css`: Poppins SemiBold 11px, 0.28em, uppercase), on every link or button drawn as a button, the header and footer included. The shared `Button` adds it to its solid and outline variants through `PublicSiteContext`, which `PPSLayout` provides (dialogs inherit it); ghost, link and icon buttons and staff screens are left as they are. Custom buttons carry the class themselves, and so do the link-in-bio pages (/amy, /rob, /sierra, /overview), which render outside `PPSLayout`. On a button, ShIFt reads "SHIFT" with its IF bold. Tags, chips, tabs, cards and text links keep their own type. Why: PPS-DEC-0028 in the PPS Ops Hub; PPS Admin, 2026-11-07, "I liked the spaced all caps cta buttons", then choosing "ShIFt becomes SHIFT" over keeping the wordmark's casing. It departs from the Brand Bible (6.6, 6.11, 4.5), as the record explains. Tests in `SiteChrome.test.tsx`.

- Public monetary text uses native CSS text highlights from useMoneyMentions and the shared detector; never mutate React text nodes. Why: prices from static copy and asynchronous content stay consistent without changing source data or link semantics.

- AI features and integration health checks use server-held Lovable AI credentials, never direct Anthropic credentials. Why: one gateway owns the app's AI access and obsolete provider secrets must not be required.

- LinkedIn article reading lives only in `supabase/functions/_shared/linkedin-article.ts`; the scanner imports through `import-linkedin-article` instead of parsing pages itself. Why: two copies of the cleanup rules drifted apart and broke imports.
- `youtube_videos` and `media_appearances` use `review_status` (pending/published); RLS hides pending from the public and public queries also filter on it. Why: scanned imports must wait for admin approval.
- Media appearance structured data uses the shared `src/lib/media-appearance-seo.mjs` builder in the public page and prerender pipeline, independent of filters and page SEO overrides. Why: crawlers and browsers must receive the same approved-only summaries.
- Public SELECT policies separate anonymous published-only reads from authenticated reviewer checks. Why: private role-check functions must not execute for anonymous visitors.
- Resource opt-ins queue email through `_shared/resource-email.ts` with explicit server credentials, report queued/suppressed/failed separately, and never block immediate access on email failure. Why: optional email copies must not gate resource access or silently claim delivery.
- Individual media pages use stable record IDs and the shared media SEO builder in React and prerender, with share-sized thumbnail copies generated at publish time. Why: per-appearance metadata must agree across browsers and social crawlers without requiring new editorial fields.
- Catalogue and relaunch SEO cleanups retain changed records in protected archive tables before retiring or clearing them. Why: editorial cleanup must remain reversible without exposing archived content publicly.
- Weekly content discovery uses one dedicated-secret callback for both scanners and pending-only imports; its scheduler credential table is service-role-only, and LinkedIn scheduled imports use the newsletter author's stable profile ID. Why: unattended discovery must not expose credentials or rely on an expiring browser session.
- Press kit media reads the existing media_appearances registry with both a published-only query and approval guard. Why: staff preview must not accidentally include pending imports or create a second media catalogue.
- The downloadable press kit is a dated static PDF in public/downloads, using existing page copy and published media only; refresh it when press materials change. Why: a same-origin file downloads reliably without adding browser PDF dependencies.
- Press forms share PressInquiryForm and submit-press-inquiry; the server fixes CRM destination IDs and email recipient, records consent on the opportunity, and only adds metadata to existing contacts. Why: unverified inquiries must not overwrite identity or let callers choose CRM destinations.
- Newsletter forms share useNewsletterSignup and submit-newsletter-optin; the server matches contacts by email, appends metadata, and preserves DND without opportunity writes or an email handoff. Why: subscriber capture stays separate from work inquiries and cannot overwrite existing identity and consent preferences.
- Work inquiry endpoints queue requester receipts through `_shared/inquiry-email.ts` after CRM save, using the shared contact-confirmation template and event-based idempotency; pages do not send their own copies. Why: closing a page must not interrupt receipt handoff or create duplicate emails.
